extracted.intended_audience: students (MIT OCW) enrolling in or consulting the 'Mathematics of Machine Learning' course
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus for an MIT course giving a mathematically rigorous introduction to machine learning: lists prerequisites, course topics (three main parts), meeting times, and assessment/assignment requirements including a final project and lecture scribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: 18.100C Real Analysis; 18.06SC Linear Algebra; 18.05 Introduction to Probability and Statistics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These courses are listed as prerequisites for this course (i.e., expected background knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Course purpose / description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a mathematically rigorous introduction to statistical and algorithmic developments in Machine Learning with emphasis on methods and their analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the pedagogical aim and tone: focus on mathematical rigor and analysis of methods rather than only applied implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics covered — Statistical Theory of Machine Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification, Regression, Aggregation; Empirical Risk Minimization, Regularization; Suprema of Empirical Processes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first of three main parts of the course; topics indicate the theoretical/statistical material students should understand and may be expected to use in assignments/projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics covered — Algorithms and Convexity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second main course part emphasizing algorithmic techniques and convex-optimization foundations relevant to machine learning methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics covered — Online Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Online Convex Optimization; Partial Information: Bandit Problems; Blackwell’s Approachability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third main part focused on sequential/online decision-making frameworks and associated theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading — Assignments / Homework
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments / Homework contribute 40% of the grade. There are 3 homework assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homework are the primary formative assessments; count and weight are specified (3 assignments total).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading — Final Project requirements and weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Final project 50% of the grade. The final project should be in any area related to one of the topics of the course or use tools that are developed in class. Examples include: implementing an algorithm for real data, extend an existing method or prove a theoretical result (or a combination of these). You will need to submit a written report (~10 pages) and give a presentation in class in the last week of semester (the duration will depend on the size of the class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable project scopes, example deliverable types (implementation, theory, extension, or combination), required deliverables (written ~10 page report and an in-class presentation), and that project constitutes half the course grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading — Lecture notes scribing
rubrics_metrics.description: Lecture notes scribing 10% of the grade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are assigned or expected to produce scribed lecture notes as part of assessment; contributes a fixed percentage to final grade.
